Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 1:

The opening of this surah is a praise-filled declaration of blessings, which shows that Allah's blessings, His generosity, and His bounties have no end. Allah's blessings are within His dominion, and there is no shortage in His kingdom. The general flow of the blessings of Allah's Being and His attributes continues throughout this entire universe, and the whole universe is glorifying Him in praise, with its echo resounding through the valleys of this boundless existence. The heart of the believer is overflowing with these blessings, and this universe descends upon the believer's heart through this Divine Book, and their manifestation is present throughout the entire universe.

﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion﴾ (76:1). He is the Owner of this universe, and He encompasses it. The forelocks of everything are in His hand; He has control over it. This is the real truth: that the King of this entire universe is Him alone. When this reality settles in the human conscience, it automatically determines its own path, and after that no one is free to worship anyone other than Allah. Then the person believes in one Master, one Deity, and one King.

﴿And He is over all things competent﴾ (76:1). Nothing can overpower Him; nothing can stand as an obstacle before His will. Beyond the limits and bounds of His will, He creates whatever He wills, does whatever He wills, and can do whatever He wills; whatever He commands, He can cause to be carried out. His power is unlimited and unrestricted. When this truth settles in the mind, then whenever any power is thought of in our feelings, imaginations, or intellect, it is negated. Whatever a human can think of, the power of Allah is greater than that. The human conception is very limited, because the human self and his intellectual universe are limited. A human is accustomed to thinking within the limited circle of his environment and knowledge, which is very restricted. The reality that Allah is competent over all things removes a person from that limited circle. When a person believes that Allah's power is unlimited, they surrender themselves to Him, and thus they move from limited thinking to unlimited thinking; otherwise a person remains a slave to the limited concept of the present and the visible.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 2:

That He is All-Powerful and carries out every kind of disposal within His dominion. So observe the signs of His power and the examples of His disposal: that He created death and life. Death includes the state that precedes giving life to any living thing, and it also includes the state that follows the withdrawal of life. Life includes the first life, and it also includes the life raised up after death. All these conditions come within the creation of Allah. The purpose of firmly establishing this reality in the human mind is that, O man, you have not been created without purpose; you are a responsible creature. It is not that you have come into being by mere chance and will simply turn to dust after dying one day. This work and this great creative process is not purposeless, but has been created to test human beings, so that, in Allah's knowledge, the display that was to come from particular people, which Allah knew in advance, comes to light, and they become deserving of appropriate reward and punishment for their deeds.

﴿Liyabluwakum ... 'amalan﴾ (76:2): "That He may test you as to which of you is best in deed." When this belief settles in the mind, a person becomes awake, cautious, alert and wise. He thinks in his heart about matters both small and great, and reflects upon both hidden and apparent things. This belief does not leave a person in heedlessness, nor does it leave him content and careless. Therefore it is said:

﴿Wa huwal-'Azizul-Ghafur﴾ (76:2): "And He is the Almighty, the Oft-Forgiving." The purpose of this concluding statement is to give assurance that Allah is indeed Qadir (All-Powerful) and 'Aziz (Almighty), but He is also Ghafur (Oft-Forgiving). He does not deal harshly with His servants. When a person firmly holds the thought that he is being tested, he remains fearful at all times as to what the outcome will be; but when he reflects that Allah is Ghafur and Rahim, hope is kindled in him, and he walks upon the Straight Path with steadiness and composure.

The concept of God that Islam presents to mankind is not one that pursues people at every moment, nor one that takes pleasure in punishing; rather, He prefers not to punish. Allah constantly reminds that you have a purpose of existence; do not let it be hidden from your sight. Raise yourself to the level of your true reality, and by means of that high station which Allah granted you when He breathed His spirit into you, prove your superiority over the rest of Allah's creation. When people attain this purpose, then the rain of Allah's mercies pours down upon them; they are assisted at every step, and in reckoning, pardon and forgiveness are exercised.

That Allah is Powerful over all things and that He created death and life so that He may test people: this reality is studied, on the one hand, in the arena of this entire universe, and on the other hand, its manifestations are shown on the field of Resurrection.

The Fire has been prepared for Satan, and for those who denied their Lord there is the punishment of Hell, and what a wretched destination it is. When they are thrown into it, they will hear its roaring, a dreadful sound, and it will be seething, almost bursting with fury. Each time a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them, "Did no warner come to you?" They will answer, "Yes, a warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, 'Allah has revealed nothing. You are only in great error.'" And they will say, "If only we had listened or understood, we would not be among the inhabitants of the blazing Fire." Thus they will themselves confess their sin. So the curse is upon the people of the Fire.

The matters mentioned in these verses are the meaning of the first verse and its examples. They are signs of the way Allah manages His kingdom and evidence of His unrestricted power. Then, in the details, there is the test of human beings and their recompense and punishment.

We cannot derive the meaning of "seven heavens, layered one above another" from present astronomical theories, because astronomical theories keep changing as our instruments of observation advance. What the verse indicates is only this: the upper universe has seven levels, separated from one another by distances, and that is why they are called layers (tabaqat).

The Quran directs our attention to the creation of the heavens and the earth and challenges human beings: look carefully at this system of the heavens and the earth, and see whether there is any flaw in it. Your observation will tire and weary you, and you will find no defect in it.

﴿You will not see any incongruity in the creation of the Most Merciful﴾ (67:3). There is no disorder, no defect, and no instability in Allah's creation.

﴿Then look again﴾ (67:3). Try again; make a sincere effort to examine it thoroughly.

﴿Do you see any crack?﴾ (67:3). Did your sight perceive any fissure, any defect, or any flaw?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 4:

ثم ارجع البصر کرتین (76 : 4) "Then return your gaze twice again" ("بار بار نگاہ دوڑاؤ"). Perhaps there is something you missed seeing, and you were unable to determine it; so cast your gaze once more.

ینقلب .................... حسیر (76 : 4) "Your gaze will return to you humbled, and it will be weary" ("تمہاری نگاہ تھک کر اور نامراد ہو کر پلٹ آئے گی"). The challenge here is this: look at these heavens and at all of Allah's creation with a more penetrating gaze, study this universe seriously, and reflect upon it. This very quality is what the Quran truly wishes to spread among people: that you should contemplate this universe deeply. In reality, this universe is extremely wondrous and exceedingly beautiful, and within it are marvels and perfections. Yet we have become so accustomed to it that its wonder has vanished from our sight, and we no longer perceive its great beauty as beauty at all. Yet it is so beautiful that the eye should never be satisfied in gazing upon its beauty, and our hearts and vision should never be sated with the lessons and signs it contains. The intellect should keep reflecting, and the varieties of its order should never come to an end. From this viewpoint, if a person studies this universe, he will find it to be a beautiful and charming exhibition arranged and adorned by Allah Ta'ala, whose novelty and beauty never grow old, because in this way its beauty will be new every day for the intellect and the gaze.

Those who know something of the reality of this universe, and who observe, in light of modern scientific knowledge, some of its aspects and how its system functions, are indeed astonished, and their intellects begin to reel. But for observing the beauty of this universe, no great quantity of knowledge is needed. It is Allah's bounty upon man that He has given him such an ability that, with ordinary observation and reflection, he can walk alongside this universe in the same way that one living person walks alongside another living person. The human heart directly receives the message of this universe and beholds its beauty, provided that he looks with lifted eyes and understands with an open heart. And he should regard this universe as a living creature and become its companion, before it reveals the secrets of this great and wondrous universe through his light of thought and his far-reaching insights.

Thus the Quran entrusts people to this universe. It places in their hands the open book of the universe, saying: listen to the voice of this universe, and take a tour of its vistas and wonders. For the addressees of the Quran are not merely scientists, but people of every age and every level. A nomad and a desert dweller reads the Quran, and so does one who lives in a city and one who travels the seas. It addresses the unlettered person who has not read even a single letter. Likewise, it addresses the astrologer and the astronomer. It speaks to the physicist and it speaks to the philosopher. Each finds in the Quran wonders, upon which he reflects, and the Quran awakens the powers of contemplation of all of them.

Like perfection, beauty is also intended for its own sake in everything in this universe; rather, perfection and beauty are two names or two aspects of one reality. In anything, perfection is itself the highest degree of its beauty. Thus the Qur'an first drew attention to the beauty of the heavens and then to their perfection.

﴿And We have adorned the nearest heaven with lamps﴾ (76:5). This is called the lowest heaven (sama-e-dunya). Perhaps this is the height that is closest to the place of the earth and to the understanding of the humans addressed by the Qur'an. By lamps and lights are meant the stars and planets that we see. The people to whom the Qur'an was addressed understood the heavens in this way when they looked at them, because they had no observatories; and even today, whoever looks at the sky with their eyes sees the stars as shining lamps.

There is no doubt that this scene is extremely beautiful, so beautiful that it captures the heart of a person. This scene has many colours: its view differs at morning and evening, and it has a separate view at sunrise and sunset. There is the dark night and the moonlight. The scenes change within a moment; they change with a change of place and change with a change of angle. But whatever scene comes before you, it grips the mind.

This single star shining on the distant horizon is, as it were, a beautiful eye that calls out with great affection. Then those two stars that appear apart are deep in conversation, away from the crowd. And that cluster of stars seen here and there is a circle of friends at the fair of the universe, which sometimes gathers here and sometimes there!

This thin crescent moon which one night is like a branch, and one night reaches its perfection, and then, falling into decline, becomes non-existent, and then is born again. Each night it has a new form.

This vast space of the universe, whose lengths and distances the sight cannot reach, and is so beautiful that the eyes keep looking. This is true beauty, whose conception a human cannot even imagine; yet if a human wishes to clothe these beauties in words, it is not possible. Human expressions fall short of it.

The Noble Qur'an draws humans' attention to the beauty of this heaven and this entire universe, because the perception of the beauty of the universe is itself a means through which a human can conceive of the beauty of the Creator of the universe. And this very perception raises a human to that lofty station which a human may ever wish to reach, because they arrive at the point beyond which they can attain eternal life. Now they arrive in a beautiful, free and everlasting world. This life is pure of the impurities of this world, and those moments of human life are everlasting moments in which a person perceives the everlasting beauty of this universe. In precisely such a state, they draw closer to the Divine Being and can conceive of the attributes of the Divine Being.

Then it is told that these beautiful stars of humanity perform another task too: as shooting stars they also bombard the devils.

﴿And We have made them missiles against the devils﴾ (67:5). In Fi Zilal al-Quran we have adopted the approach of keeping discussion of unseen matters within the limit to which the Qur'an has spoken. In this matter, we remain confined to the aspect the Qur'an has described. What the Qur'an has said is a complete statement.

Our belief is that there is a creation called Satan and devils; some attributes of these devils are mentioned in the Qur'an. The subject has already been discussed in Zilal al-Quran, and there is no need for further addition to it. Our belief is also that when these devils try to ascend to the higher realm, shooting stars drive them away, as another place says:

﴿And We guarded it from every rebellious devil... except one who steals a hearing, and he is pursued by a piercing flame﴾ (72:8–10). 

How the shooting star pursues, how large this star is, and what its form is: God has not told us these details, and humans have no other source of knowledge through which such matters can be asked. It is enough to be content with what the Qur'an has said, and this is what is intended here. If God had intended to tell more, He would have told. Therefore, one should not pursue that which God has not regarded as a source of goodness and blessing for us. The stoning of devils is also among such matters, of which we have not been given detailed knowledge. Apart from the punishment of shooting stars in this world, they have another punishment in the Hereafter.

﴿And We have prepared for them the punishment of the blazing fire﴾ (67:5). This bombardment is in the world, and the punishment of fire in the Hereafter.

Surah Al-Mulk (67), verse 6: ﴿And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (76 : 6)

After this, the details of a scene of Hell are given, in which Hell appears in a state of extreme wrath and vengeance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 7:

﴿When they are cast into it, they will hear its roaring terrible sound while it boils up, almost bursting with fury﴾ (76:8). Behold Hell: it is like a living creature. It is angry, it struggles to contain its rage, its breathing heaves, and its breath takes on the form of a hissing snarl out of its fury. It is under such pressure from its anger, loathing and hatred that it seems about to burst.

Apparently this manner of expression is a figurative portrayal. But the deeper we study this universe, the more we find that every creature of Allah is alive and has a particular soul of its own. Every creature knows its Lord, glorifies Him and praises Him. When every creature of Allah sees man disbelieving in the Lord, all creatures become frightened, because everything has recognition of its Creator and everything is obedient to His command. Therefore everything feels anger at the disobedient creature, and the souls of all creatures hate every denier.

The Qur'an says:

﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is in them glorify Him. There is not a thing but that it exalts His praise, but you do not understand their glorification﴾ (17:44). And similarly concerning Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him):

﴿O mountains, sing with him, and so too the birds﴾ (34:10).

And elsewhere it is explicitly stated:

﴿Then He turned to the heaven when it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly, in obedience"﴾ (41:11).

All these things point to the reality that everything believes in the Lord, glorifies Him and praises Him. When these things see that man disobeys the Creator of the universe, they become terrified. When man adopts a different attitude, these things tremble in fear of the wrath of Allah. They become so angry that, because of the intensity of their wrath, they are about to attack man with a crash. It is like when someone abuses a noble and self-respecting person: his throat chokes with rage, his breath heaves, and he struggles with great difficulty to control himself. Such is the condition of Hell that has been described.

﴿It seethes and almost bursts with fury﴾ (67:8).

The Qur'anic quotation in this passage is 67:8 itself, which the commentary cites as part of its discussion; the verse text here is the Qur'anic phrase ﴿كلما ألقي فيها فوج سألهم خزنتها ألم يأتكم نذير﴾ (76:8 as cited in the source).

Translation:

Likewise will be the condition of the keepers of Hell as well.

﴿Whenever a group is cast into it, its keepers will ask them: "Did no warner come to you?"﴾ (76:8)

It is clear that this question, when put to them in Hell, is not asked for the purpose of seeking information. It is asked in order to rebuke them and to silence them with argument. In effect, the keepers of Hell also share in that wrath along with Hell itself. Just as both of those are involved in punishing them, so too, if a wretched and distressed person is struck with reproaches and scourges of rebuke, the bitterness he feels knows no bounds. But listen to the reply of these people, and see how abjectly humiliated they have become. Now they admit their heedlessness and folly like children who have been caught out, whereas previously they had arrogantly called the Messengers misguided.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verses 9–10:

[Qutb's text continues from the previous verses:] "They will say, 'Yes! A warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, "Allah has revealed nothing; you are only in great error."'" And they will say, "If only we had listened or understood, we would not now be among the companions of the blazing Fire." Thus they will confess their own sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze!

Whoever listens and tries to understand the matter with reason does not put himself in that position, nor does he deny in the way those wretched people denied. He does not dare to reject the messengers of truth, nor does he accuse them of misguidance in such a crude manner, without any reasonable cause. Rather, he does not claim that Allah has revealed nothing and that you are lying, as though he himself had just come from Allah's presence.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verses 9–10:

[Qutb's text continues from the previous verses:] "They will say, 'Yes! A warner did come to us, but we denied him and said, "Allah has revealed nothing; you are only in great error."'" And they will say, "If only we had listened or understood, we would not now be among the companions of the blazing Fire." Thus they will confess their own sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze!

Whoever listens and tries to understand the matter with reason does not put himself in that position, nor does he deny in the way those wretched people denied. He does not dare to reject the messengers of truth, nor does he accuse them of misguidance in such a crude manner, without any reasonable cause. Rather, he does not claim that Allah has revealed nothing and that you are lying, as though he himself had just come from Allah's presence.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verse 11:

﴿So they will acknowledge their sin. So away with the companions of the Blaze!﴾ (76:11) Thus they will themselves confess their wrongdoing; a curse upon those people of the Fire.

Suhq (سحق) means distance. This is an invocation of ruin upon them from Allah. When they made this confession, and made it at the time when that scene stood before them, the reality of which they had been denying, then when Allah pronounces a curse upon someone, it is as though their destruction has been decided. These people have been removed far from the mercy of Allah; now they have no hope of Allah's forgiveness, nor any hope of escaping the punishment. Now they are the companions of the Fire. What an evil companionship, what an evil fellowship is theirs, and what an evil end!

This punishment, the punishment of Hell, which is hurling curses at them, is a severe punishment, a terrifying punishment. Allah does not wrong anyone. The truth is that Allah has placed within every soul the reality of faith and the proofs of faith; yet even despite this, if any soul denies Allah, it becomes evident that there is no goodness within it, and it is deprived of every kind of goodness. In the same way, it loses the weight of all the fundamental qualities of its existence and personality. It is like stones being burned in Hell. Its personality has cast itself down from its own dwelling into that Fire, whereas its duty was to flee from it.

Whoever denies Allah, instead of advancing, turns back on his heels and falls on his face, and he keeps falling in every race of life, until he takes on the most wretched, backward and detestable form. Eventually he takes on the form of a loathsome inhabitant of Hell. He becomes so ugly that nothing in this world is as repulsive in appearance as he is, like something that has been disfigured. Then, apart from such a soul, the entire universe stands on one side. Everything is a believer, a praiser of Allah, and everything contains goodness, and among all things there is a bond of faith. Except for those human and satanic souls that adopt disbelief, every relationship of these denying and misguided individuals, wherever they may be, is severed from everything except Hell; they are of no use for anything. Within them there is no meaning, no truth and no honour. Therefore such souls become deserving of Hell.

The manner of the Qur'an is to present contrasting qualities. Just as the scenes of the people of Hell were shown, in contrast the conditions of the believers are also shown. This is the style of the entire Qur'an. Accordingly, here too the verses ...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 12:

ان الذین ................ اجرکبیر

"Ghayb" (the unseen) here means that they have not seen their Lord yet they fear Him, and it also means that they fear their Lord even in a state in which no one is watching them. When a person does not commit evil even in secret, his conscience is alive, and he is truly a believer in God.

Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar has narrated in his Musnad, from Talut ibn Abbad, from Harith ibn Ubayd, from Thabit, from Anas, who said: The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) asked: "O Messenger of Allah, we are in one state when we are with you, but when we are apart from you our state becomes different." He (ﷺ) said: "What is your relationship with your Lord?" They said: "Our Lord is our Lord in solitude and in gatherings, everywhere." He (ﷺ) said: "This is not hypocrisy." Therefore, the connection with Allah is a true connection. When one has certainty in Allah, such a person is a believer.

This verse, mentioned above, joins the preceding and following themes together: that Allah has knowledge of every state, whether something is apparent or hidden, in solitude or otherwise. Allah the Exalted calls out to people, saying: I created you, and I am aware of both your outward and inward being; I know all the capacities of My creation.

"Whether you conceal your speech or proclaim it, He indeed knows what is in the breasts."

Wait, I need to translate the passage as given. Here it is:

Verse 13 of Surah al-Mulk: ﴿And whether you keep your speech secret or declare it aloud, indeed He is All-Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ (67:13)

Sayyid Qutb's commentary: You may conceal a matter or make it public; Allah has knowledge of it. He knows the open, the hidden, and what is in the hearts.

Indeed He knows the secrets of hearts (76:31)? The Qur'anic quotation ﴿He knows well the contents of the breasts﴾ (76:31 is cited as "He knows the contents of hearts"). The thing that has not yet left the heart and reached the mouth. For He is the One who created these matters within the hearts, just as He created the hearts themselves.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verse 14:

﴿Does He not know who He has created?﴾ (76:41)

﴿And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾ (76:41). His knowledge reaches to the finest and the most hidden depths. Everything concealed and veiled is within His knowledge.

Those who hide some action from Allah, or hide words from Allah, or think about the intention of the heart that "this is only an intention," hold a ridiculous notion. In whose hand is the conscience in which they conceal such things? It is in the hand of Allah. He knows every wave of thought that rises within it. Intention and resolve are also part of Allah's creation, and He knows who intends what. He knows what people conceal and what they do not conceal.

The Qur'an wishes to fix this reality in the human heart, because in this way people can truly grasp the Great Reality. Moreover, their sense of vigilance and God-consciousness (taqwa) grows, and this is connected with the great responsibility that they have taken up in this world: spreading the correct way of life in the world, establishing justice, and attaining sincerity in intention and action. No human can reach this station unless he fears God both outwardly and inwardly, and Allah is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware.

When a believer reaches this station, he fears Allah in his secret intentions, fears the hidden whispers within his heart, and fears his outward speech and deeds if they are contrary to the pleasure of Allah, for Allah is aware of every whisper.

After this, the discourse turns from the subject of human souls and their monitoring to the earth, that it was created for human beings, that this earth has been made subservient to you, and that all things have been created for your sake.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 15:

﴿He it is who made the earth subservient to you, so walk in its tracts and eat of His provision; and to Him is the resurrection.﴾

The condition of people is that, because they live on this earth, and because every kind of living provision is available to them on it, and because of their ability to move about in it and their access to its soil, water, air and other treasures, and because they use all its produce, they have become accustomed to life here. They have even forgotten that Allah has made it subservient to them and placed it at their disposal. The Qur'an repeatedly reminds them of this lesson: reflect on this, and see. Thus in every age people have understood the meaning of the subjugation of the universe according to their own knowledge.

For the early listeners, a subservient earth conveyed only this meaning: that we can walk upon this earth, on foot or riding horses, or on a ship that cleaves the breast of the sea; that we can cultivate it; and that we can use whatever living and dead creatures it contains: water, air, earth and every kind of vegetation.

These were the general meanings which science has now made somewhat more detailed. As far as our knowledge has advanced today, and because of this knowledge, the meaning of this Qur'anic text has also become broader, and future generations will understand it even more.

Now, according to modern sciences, how vast is its meaning? The word *dhalul* (ذلول, tame, docile) is generally used for an animal that has been trained, that is good for riding and obedient. We now clearly understand that the application of this word to the earth means that this earth is also a mount. If it were still, calm and fixed, it would be one thing; but in reality it is a moving mount, indeed an extremely fast-moving one. Allah has made it so obedient an animal that it does not throw its rider off, nor does it blow him into the air. Human footsteps do not stagger upon it, and it does not jolt, shake or toss its rider as an unbroken animal, or a pot or camel with a rider, would do. Moreover, it is an animal that, like a docile beast, also gives milk.

This animal, or this sphere on which we are riding, spins around itself at about one thousand miles per hour, and along with this axial speed it also races around the sun at about 56 thousand miles per hour. Then this earth, the sun, and the whole galaxy of the sun move at 02 thousand miles per hour toward the direction of the constellation Orion (VAST ORBITA) in the sky, whose one circuit is completed in 62 crore years (620 million years). Despite all these speeds, despite all these races, we sit very comfortably on the back of this horse, and this horse is a very great *dhalul*. It proceeds with such calm that we do not even feel its speed. It sits very peacefully. There is no pressure on its nerves, and it does not happen that we fall from it and our bodies are scattered throughout this universe. And from this horse a human being never falls.

Then this horse is harnessed in three different motions. Of these, two motions, namely the axial motion and the solar motion, we know the effects of. They have an effect on humans, on the earth, and on the life found on this earth. Because of the axial rotation of the earth, night and day come into being. If there were always night, all things would freeze from the cold; and its orbit around the sun determines the seasons and the times of the various harvests. And if there were only one season, the present form of the earth would not exist. As for the third motion, we have not yet come to know its wisdom, and it is necessary that it be related to some greater system of this great universe. And Allah knows best!

This horse, which is simultaneously making these various motions, remains fixed in its place, or appears to be fixed. And it is tilted on its axis at 23.5 degrees. As a result of this tilt, four different seasons come into being. These seasons arise from the earth's solar revolution. If there were even a slight disturbance in this motion, our entire seasonal system, the system of rains, the system of the growth of crops, and the system of months and years would be destroyed; indeed, it is possible that life itself would disappear from the earth.

Allah has made the earth tame for humans in such a way that it has placed within it such a measure of gravitational attraction that the earth keeps humans stuck to its surface, and during all its motions humans do not roll about on it. Likewise, a system of atmospheric pressure has been established upon it, because of which humans can walk upon it with ease. If the present atmospheric pressure were even slightly greater, it would be impossible for humans to walk upon the earth, or walking would be extremely difficult. With greater pressure, humans would be pressed down and unable to walk. And if the present pressure were reduced even somewhat, humans would go leaping about in the air and their footsteps would become unsteady, or their stomachs would burst from internal pressure, and their eardrums would rupture, just as happens to those who go into the upper atmosphere and are not provided with the artificial atmospheric pressure that exists here.

Then Allah subjugated the present earth. He made its surface level and provided soft soil upon it from above. If this earth were like a hard desert, as scientists have assumed, that it cooled and became a rock, then walking upon it would also be difficult, and there would be no growth within it at all. But atmospheric factors, air, heat, cold and rains, broke and shattered those hard stones, and in this way the soil came into being on the earth, within which every kind of produce is possible (and from it humans too were created). Thus those who ride this mount also drink its milk.

And Allah made the earth subservient in such a way that, upon it, in the air that He gathered over it, He assembled all the necessities of humans and of all other life. And He placed these necessities within that air with such precision that if any of these elements were increased or decreased even slightly, all life would end from the surface of the globe. The proportion of oxygen in the air is 12 (per cent), nitrogen is 87%, the rest is carbon dioxide, and there are other gases. And this proportion is indispensable for the sustenance of life on earth.

Then Allah made the earth suitable for the thousands of needs of human life. Among these, the present size of the earth, the present size of the sun, and the present size of the moon are all favourable. Then the present distance of the earth from the sun and moon, the temperature of the sun, the present thickness of the earth's crust, the present speed of the earth, the earth's being tilted to one side on its axis, then the present ratio of land to water, the present density of the air, and other things of this kind, all together make the earth subservient to humans and tame for them. And because of these things, the provision of humans has been made available, and through them various animals, and then life has been given to humans.

This Qur'anic verse points to these matters so that every person of every age may understand it according to his scientific capacity. As human observation advances, the meaning of the verse will broaden, and humanity will continually renew the awareness that all sovereignty is in the hand of Allah. He is the guardian of every thing, and He is the guardian of every thing in the whole environment of humans. This earth has been made subservient for humans. Allah protects humans, and if at any time His guardianship were lifted, this entire system would instantly fall into disorder.

When this understanding settled into the human conscience, Allah, the Most Merciful and the Most Compassionate, commanded: walk upon the breast of this earth and use the provisions that are placed within it.

﴿Walk upon its shoulders and eat of His provision﴾ (76:51). *Manakib* (مناکب) means its heights or its sides. When Allah permitted walking upon the heights and sides of the earth, the permission to walk in its plains and its valleys was also included, and whatever provision is within it is the creation of Allah. It is not anyone's property, to be in someone's hand; all of it belongs to His dominion. Its meaning is very broad, far beyond what generally comes to people's minds upon the word *rizq* (provision). It does not mean only wealth that is in someone's possession so that he may fulfil his needs with it. The provision here means all the things that are causes of sustenance for humans and that are deposited within this earth: all the elements from which this earth was made, and all the elements which Allah made the vegetation, animals and humans fit to use. Modern sciences have explained this provision well; briefly, its nature is as follows:

"The life of every plant depends upon the tiny particles, molecules, of carbon dioxide present in the air. The plant takes these in by breathing, and this is a chemical process completed in sunlight. It should be understood that the leaves of trees are in fact the lungs of trees. In sunlight, plants become capable of absorbing carbon dioxide, separating carbon from oxygen, releasing the oxygen back, and combining carbon with hydrogen, which the plant takes up through its roots in the form of water (where the oxygen and hydrogen of water are separated), and then, in an astonishingly wondrous way, nature produces from these elements sugar, organic fibres and many other chemical substances, from which fruits and flowers are produced, and from which the plant takes its own nourishment and also produces food for all the other animals on the surface of the earth. And during this process the plant expels the oxygen that it draws in, without which life would end within five seconds."

"Similarly, it appears that all vegetation, all forests, all shrubs, the algae found on water, and all crops are in fact formed from carbon and water. Animals and humans release carbon dioxide, and vegetation releases oxygen. If this exchange did not take place, human life and animal life would eventually exhaust all the oxygen and all the carbon dioxide, and when this balance ended, the plants would be scorched and humans would die. Recently it has been discovered that a small quantity of carbon dioxide is necessary for the life of animals, while plants also need a small quantity of oxygen."

"Although we do not absorb hydrogen through breathing, its existence is also necessary, because without it water does not exist, and water is so essential for human and animal life and for plants that without it the life of humans and animals is simply impossible." (*Science Calls to Faith*, trans. Mahmud Salih Falaki, pp. 20, 12.)

Likewise, nitrogen also has a deep connection with the provision of the earth.

"No food plant can grow without nitrogen. It must somehow obtain nitrogen. There are two ways by which nitrogen enters agricultural soil. First, a special kind of bacteria (microbes) live in the roots of leguminous plants, such as clover, chickpeas, beans and the like. These bacteria take pure nitrogen, that is, from the air, and release it into the soil in a compound form, and then the plant can absorb it into itself. When this plant dies, this compound nitrogen remains within the soil."

"There is a second way by which nitrogen enters the soil: when winds blow in which lightning flashes. Whenever lightning flashes within the winds, it unites some oxygen and nitrogen, and the rain throws it down upon the earth as a compound nitrogen, in a form that plants can absorb."

Because plants cannot absorb pure nitrogen into themselves, since in the air its proportion is 87%. (*Science Calls to Faith*, trans. Mahmud Salih Falaki, pp. 20, 12.)

And whatever solid and liquid provision exists within the earth, all of it, the earth and its conditions, is connected with the provision.

There is no need here for explanations of the provisions within, because the word *rizq* (provision) here has a very broad and very deep meaning. And when Allah permits us, saying, walk in the earth and seek provision, because the earth has been made subservient for you, then all of this falls within the meaning of that word, and we are permitted to benefit from it as much as humans are able to.

﴿Walk upon its shoulders and eat of His provision﴾ (76:51).

But this permission is for a determined time, and the time has been fixed, and it is known to Allah. It accords with Allah's governance of the universe. Eat until the period of trial of life and death; but after that...

﴿And to Him is the resurrection﴾ (76:51). To Him you must go, and if you do not accept this, then tell: to whom else should you go? There is no refuge anywhere other than Him, and He has power over all things.

While humans were still enjoying the blessings of Allah upon the back of this earth and within it, and were gathering blessings by walking on the earth by the command of Allah, suddenly a tremor arises within this tamed and obedient earth, and its balance and its motion are instantly disrupted. Now this same calm earth is bombarding them and bringing down mountains upon them. An earthquake is set up in their feelings and imaginations, so that these people are not absorbed merely in the comfort of the earth and in enjoying its blessings, but also look at the King who established this system, and keep their hearts and thoughts connected with Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verses 16–17:

﴿Are you secure that He who is in the heaven ........ [ellipsis as in the source] ........ My warning?﴾

This human being, who rides upon this tamed and obedient mount and enjoys its comforts, and who obtains his sustenance from it in the form of milk, knows that this obedient mount will one day go out of control. When Allah's command comes, it will no longer remain as it is. It will give only a slight jolt, and everything upon it will be scattered here and there. The mountains will tremble like tufts of cotton, and it will begin to lurch with such violent force. Such conditions occur during great earthquakes and great volcanic eruptions, which show how much rebellion lies within this restrained and subservient earth, a rebellion that cannot be controlled. Its reins are held by Allah. Therefore it does not lurch. But when it gives jolts, even for a few seconds or a minute, every strong and sturdy fortress that people have built upon the earth is demolished. Entire towns sink into its belly, and when people are going into it, nothing can save them.

At the time of earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and sinking, these Pharaonic humans then run here and there like rats, just as rats run about in a cage trying to escape. A minute before, they were heedless, intoxicated, rebellious, and oblivious of that exalted Being who had held the reins of this rebellious mount. Now there is confusion on every side.

In this world, humans also see storms that rain stones along with clouds and rain, and as they pass through every town, they carry away trees, tents and houses. They burn forests to ashes, and people are left only watching. They watch helplessly. Their knowledge, their power and their technology remain just as they were, useless. These storms travel at speeds of thousands of miles, uprooting stones and pushing seas onto dry land, and humans stand before them like a mosquito or an ant. Yet it is the power of Allah that holds back His armies, and then this earth and this mount become settled.

The Holy Qur'an reminds humans that this mount, which has been tamed for you and travels in great safety, should not deceive you. It is under the control of the Creator of the universe, and it is He who has tamed it for you. When its rebellions begin, you will not be able to save yourselves in any way. This earth can lurch and can gather great speed. It can also spew out hot, molten lava from within itself. It can sink you into the earth, and there can be a rain of stones. No human power can stop it, nor can any human power avert its destruction and ruin. Allah warns in such a way that hearts tremble, nerves become numb, and limbs begin to shake.

﴿Then you will know how My warning was﴾ (76:71).

Now, before them is placed a general indication of historical events: the dreadful end of some deniers in past ages is before you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verses 16–17:

﴿Are you secure that He who is in the heaven ........ [ellipsis as in the source] ........ My warning?﴾

This human being, who rides upon this tamed and obedient mount and enjoys its comforts, and who obtains his sustenance from it in the form of milk, knows that this obedient mount will one day go out of control. Yet it is the power of Allah that holds back His armies, and then this earth and this mount become settled.

The Holy Qur'an reminds humans that this mount, which has been tamed for you and travels in great safety, should not deceive you. It is under the control of the Creator of the universe, and it is He who has tamed it for you. When its rebellions begin, you will not be able to save yourselves in any way. This earth can lurch and can gather great speed. It can also spew out hot, molten lava from within itself. It can sink you into the earth, and there can be a rain of stones. No human power can stop it, nor can any human power avert its destruction and ruin. Allah warns in such a way that hearts tremble, nerves become numb, and limbs begin to shake.

﴿Then you will know how My warning was﴾ (76:71).

Now, before them is placed a general indication of historical events: the dreadful end of some deniers in past ages is before you.

And those before them had denied, so see how terrible My punishment was. (76 : 81) ... The word nakir (disapproval, punishment) means anger, rebuke, and the punishment that follows from it. They know the events in which Allah seized earlier nations, and they are asked: tell us yourselves how the seizing was.

﴿Then see how was My nakir (disapproval and punishment).﴾ (76 : 81), because the traces were before their eyes. So they would know what the punishment was like.

Here Allah warns against a kind of heedlessness, a sense of security in which a person forgets Allah. This is the kind of security that removes from the heart the fear of Allah's power and the awareness of His greatness. The peace and tranquillity meant here is not the state that a person gains through the remembrance of Allah, which comes from certainty in Allah's mercy and His protection. The believer hopes for Allah's mercy and grace, but is not heedless. The believer who remembers Allah keeps his gaze always turned toward Him, is modest before Him, fears His wrath, and always prays: "O Allah, protect me from the hardship You have written for me in Your decree, and grant me well-being." He is always fearful.

Imam Ahmad, with his chain of narration, reports from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: "I never saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laugh in a carefree way, so that his uvula could be seen. He would only smile. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was such that when he saw a cloud or a strong wind, the effect would show on his face. So I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, when people see a cloud or the wind, they rejoice, hoping that rain will come, but I see that when you see these things, signs of aversion appear on your face.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, 'O Aisha, what guarantee is there that it does not contain the punishment of Allah? Some nations were punished by wind. A people saw the punishment and said, "This is a cloud that will bring us rain."'" (Sahihain, i.e., Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim)

This is a constant, awakened awareness of Allah and of the system of His decree and destiny. It is also reported from the Prophet's (ﷺ) noble conduct in the hadith. This awareness does not conflict with tranquillity in Allah's mercy or with hope in His grace.

Thus the verses show that all apparent causes have one Causer of causes. All causes are traced back to the First Cause, who is the Divine Being, in whose hand is all sovereignty and who has power over everything. Therefore the sinking of a village into the earth, the bringing of a people into the path of a volcano, the destruction of a town by earthquake, and the exposure of a town to violent winds are solely within the power of Allah. Apart from Him, are all these cosmic forces and physical forces in the hands of any human being? Their affair is in Allah's hand. The causes that people list regarding them are mere assumptions by which humans try to give a reasonable explanation of these events, but in these events they have no role or action, and they cannot protect themselves from them. The changes that humans bring upon the surface of this earth are destroyed in a single jolt. A storm rises in which there is fire, and it reduces them to ashes. It is as if they were a paper game. Therefore people should refer every matter solely to the Creator of the universe, consider Him the first cause of all events, consider Him the one who sets in motion the laws of nature by which the universe is run, and turn toward the sky, for the sky is the symbol of height. Thus they should remember Allah, in whose hand are all kingdoms, and who has power over all things.

The power within a human being is what the Creator has given him. The knowledge he has is what the Creator has given him. But the reins of this whole universe are in Allah's hand. The laws of this universe are made by Allah, and the forces within it exist by Allah's support. These forces operate according to Allah's system of decree and destiny. The hardship that reaches a person from them, the blessings that reach him from them, and the events and calamities that from time to time befall him in this universe are all from Allah. As for the great calamities that befall a person in this world, before which a person stands helpless and suffers enormous loss, the only response a person can make is to remember Allah, the Creator of the universe, and to raise his hands in prayer before Him, who has made these forces subject to humans, and to seek help from Allah alone that He make these forces subject to him.

When a person forgets this truth, is deceived by pride, and boasts that he has subdued some forces of this universe, such a person in reality moves away from true knowledge, and his connection with true knowledge is cut off, although this true knowledge would raise him to the highest source. Thus he is humbled and falls to the earth, whereas the person who has true knowledge, who is a sincere believer, bows his head. But he reaches the vast fair of this universe, and his connection with the Divine Being is established. This is the mercy of Allah, the taste of which only the one upon whom it has been bestowed can enjoy, and this mercy of Allah rests upon the one for whom Allah has written it.

But however much a person may be arrogant, the forces of this universe compel him to acknowledge his helplessness with humility, whether or not he has tasted true knowledge. He makes new discoveries and subdues new natural forces, but when he then confronts the rebellious cosmic forces, he accepts his incapacity and admits it with complete humiliation. It is true that sometimes he hides from a violent storm in some shelter, but this storm passes over him with great violence and cannot stop his path. At most he can avoid the storm's reach, but even this only occasionally. Sometimes these forces are so rebellious that they destroy him behind walls and inside cellars. And sometimes, when he encounters the rage of the sea, large ships sink amid the waves and whirlwinds, appearing as if they were a child's game. As for earthquakes and volcanoes, they have been uncontrollable from the first day until today. Only blindness of the intellect can make a person believe that he can remain here alone without Allah, or that he is the owner of this universe.

The truth is that the human being is the vicegerent and successor of Allah on this earth, and he has been given knowledge, power, and capability only to the extent that Allah willed. The truth is that his protector and guardian here is Allah alone. He is the Provider and the Giver. If the hand of Allah's power were to withdraw its protection from him even for a moment, the natural forces of this world would crush him within a second, and even flies and ants alone would devour him. But he is safe and honored here by Allah's command. Therefore he should know where this dignity and nobility come from. It is the grace of Allah that has been given to him.

Now, after warning and admonition, he is again invited to reflect, in a scene that he sees often, indeed sees all the time, yet a human being rarely reflects upon it. Yet that scene is a great manifestation of the power of Allah, and if he reflects upon it, he can learn much from it, for it is a wondrous effect among the signs of Allah's power.

Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is the All-Seer of everything. (Qur'an 67:19)

This miraculous phenomenon, which occurs constantly, is not regarded as significant by us, because it happens repeatedly. We also forget the power of Allah operating within it. Especially when they fly in formation, spreading their wings and folding them, in both cases they fly in ranks. And these birds sometimes perform feats that reveal the beauty of their creation. A person is left gazing. This is a wondrous spectacle among Allah's amazing creations, in which perfection and beauty are seen together. The Qur'an's reference to this scene is this:

﴿Have they not seen the birds above them, spreading and folding their wings?﴾ (67:19). After this it is pointed out who has designed them.

﴿None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ (67:19). The Most Merciful has kept them in the air according to the laws of nature that Allah has set for the air, and within these laws there is a wondrous order. According to these laws Allah has created these birds, in which the account of every cell and every particle is preserved. These are the laws by which thousands of equational formulas operate in the atmosphere so that the flight of birds in the air may be completed, and continue to run with such order.

And the Most Merciful has kept these birds in this state by His mighty power, and His sight and watch over them is always present and is never absent for a moment. It is Allah who keeps these laws and formulas in this universe constantly established, balanced and organised. These principles never break down at any time. They never suffer disruption, and never fall into disorder, not even for the blink of an eye, at any time.

﴿None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ (67:19): it is the Most Merciful alone who holds them thus, so that every bird and every feather is held by Allah. And when this bird folds its wings in the air, it then hangs suspended in the atmosphere, and Allah is keeping it there.

﴿Indeed He is the All-Seer of everything﴾ (67:19). He sees everything and is aware of everything. He prepares the circumstances of life for it, gives it strength, and at every moment supplies its needs, its daily needs. As one who is All-Knowing and All-Seeing does, He keeps the birds in the air in the same way that He keeps all animals on the earth, those that fly in the air. Just as in this cosmos He has held back great celestial bodies, and none but Allah holds them back. But the Qur'an seizes people and draws their eyes and hearts to all the scenes that they can see and understand, and impresses upon their hearts the hints and effects of those scenes. Otherwise, every work of Allah carries a miracle, and every creature bears His signs, and every species can see Him according to its own understanding. A Bedouin used to say:

"The dropping shows the camel" (al-Ba'ra tadullu 'ala al-ba'ir): the camel's dung indicates that a camel has passed by. And today a human being, through his observations and by Allah's grace, knows everything, or much of it.

Now the Qur'an brings them back to those circumstances in which they are helpless: storms, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and showers of stones. Look at the bird floating in the air: they are in safety in the expanse of the cosmos by Allah's grace. So they are reminded again of their difficult moments, and the repetition of this has a great effect.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verse 20:

"Or who is there that could be an army for you to help you apart from the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are only in delusion." (The Quranic portion as quoted in the commentary: امن ھذا ... فی غرور)

Note: The Urdu text begins with a truncated Quranic quotation, and I have rendered the Quranic words as they appear in the source, followed by the commentary.

"Allah previously warned mankind of being swallowed up by the earth (khasf), while many deniers before them had been given this punishment. Then He warned them of being stoned, while many had been stoned. And in the same way He warned them of various other destructions that befell the other deniers. Here they are asked again: who is there apart from Allah who helps them and protects them from these various kinds of destruction? Who, apart from the Most Merciful, can hold back Allah's grip?"

﴿Indeed, the disbelievers are only in delusion﴾ (67:20). This delusion makes them feel secure, as though they are under someone's guarantee and protection, although they have already become deserving of Allah's wrath and punishment. This is because they have neither believed nor done righteous deeds, which are the means by which Allah's mercy descends and His punishment is averted.

Once again, with a gentle nudge, they are made to realise that if Allah were to withhold this provision of His, which has been mentioned above, then who is there who could make such a great arrangement?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 21:

As has already passed, every human being depends on the causes (asbab) that Allah has created. If Allah were to withdraw any one of these causes, people would die of hunger. Allah has placed this provision within the scheme of this universe as a chain of causes. All these causes are such that they are not within human power, yet they are within the reach of all human beings. All these causes were created even before the existence of man. In their natural power and strength, these causes are far greater than man, and if even one of them were erased by the hand of divine power, all of mankind would be wiped off the face of the earth.

If Allah were to stop the water, or block the air, or remove the elements from which things are made, then who could bring it back? There are stars a thousand times larger than the earth, yet they are empty of life and the causes of life.

Within this deep, wide and great meaning, all the meanings of the word rizq (provision) are contained. The provision which man believes he earns for himself, for example through labour, through invention, through obtaining produce, depends upon certain causes and elements, and also upon the nations to whom Allah has given those causes from another direction. For a worker who breathes and who moves, does so only by virtue of the provision of Allah. It is Allah who created this worker, gave him power and strength, gave him a soul which breathes in this world, then through the material that flows within his body he obtains strength and moves, and the intellectual work he performs, he is able to perform only because of the intellectual faculty which Allah placed in his brain. And whatever a craftsman or inventor creates, he uses material created by Allah. And in this process too, man uses human and cosmic causes which are the provision and gift of Allah.

﴿Say: Who is there that can provide for you if the Most Merciful withholds His provision?﴾ (67:21)

﴿Nay, but they persist in arrogance and aversion.﴾ (67:21)

Having established that provision comes from Allah alone, it is said that these people turn away and act arrogantly, and with great pride they hate the call to Islam, although they live upon the provision of Allah. Therefore, to eat the provision of Allah and then act with rebellion, and in pride turn away from religion, is an extremely vile and base act, since all their needs are based on the grace and bounty of Allah. And yet they still turn away and act with arrogance.

This is the picture of those who reject the call of Allah, in a state of pride and rebellion and with intense arrogant hatred. They forget that they are creatures of Allah, that they have lived by the grace and bounty of Allah, and that they are not even the owners of their own existence or the necessities of their lives.

Despite these circumstances, they used to claim about the companions of the Prophet ﷺ that they were misguided people, while they considered themselves to be upon guidance. And in every age this is how those who call people to God are regarded, so the true reality of such claimants and of the believers is presented in the form of a parable or a scene.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 67, verse 22:

"Is one who walks prone (upside down) on his face better guided, or one who walks upright on a straight path? ..." [Qur'an 67:22]

The one who walks prone is of two kinds. The first is one who does not walk upright on his feet but crawls on his face, although Allah created feet for walking. Or it may mean that he stumbles along the way, falls, gets up and walks, then falls on his face again, and is never granted a straight gait. This is the state of the wretched person who endures hardship and suffering, keeps stumbling and falling, and is also deprived of the destination. By contrast, the believer walks upright on a straight highway at a balanced pace; the path is clear, continuous, and certainly leads to the destination.

The first state belongs to a wretched, misguided and rebellious person. He is deprived of the path of Allah and of His guidance. He is deprived of the laws of nature established by Allah; he collides with the principles of nature and is at odds with the creatures of God. This is because he walks on a wrong path and does not take the straight way. He travels on wrong trails which contain rises and falls and a stony road. He keeps falling, covers the road with great hardship, and remains in perpetual error.

The second is the person who is righteous, serious, aware of the way of God, who walks upon it, and who keeps the correct pace in accordance with the laws of nature established by Allah. He is on a straight, continuous road, upon which the caravan of faith moves forward with its host, its equipment and its provisions, and upon which the whole caravan of creation of this universe moves forward, whether living or non-living!

The life of faith is in fact ease, facility and steadfastness; there is tranquility on straight paths. The life of disbelief is hardship, falling and stumbling, walking prone, and walking on wrong paths.

Then let every person reflect on which of these two paths is right. Is an answer needed? No, the answer is contained within the question itself. It is a question that affirms and confirms that the matter is indeed so.

This question and answer concludes when our imagination runs after the picture and parable of these two individuals. One group walks prone on its face, falls, rises, then falls again, on a stony road, a crooked road, a thorny road. Its destination is unknown; it only falls and rises. Each one runs on his own, whereas the other group walks together in the form of a caravan, moving forward in step, upon a straight path, a highway, and their destination is one: everyone is heading in that direction.

This is the Qur'anic manner of discourse, which places abstract, philosophical truths before our eyes in a very embodied and concrete manner, so that meanings appear to be walking and moving.

[Then Qur'an 67:23 onward:] "Say: It is He who brought you into being and made for you hearing, sight and hearts; little is it that you give thanks." ... (67:23) After mentioning guidance and misguidance, the verses now show them the means Allah has given them for guidance and misguidance, namely the natural faculties through which they can perceive realities, which they did not make use of and for which they did not give thanks.

Qul huwa .................... tashkurun

It is an established fact that Allah alone created man, and it was Allah who gave him the faculties of sight, hearing and thought. It is also an undeniable truth that among the creatures of Allah, man is a supreme and exalted creature, and that he exists in this world. He did not create himself, so there must exist something higher, more exalted and more knowing than him. And He is the Creator. No one can escape acknowledging the Creator, because the very existence of man itself demands that some exalted power exists, and to argue and dispute about it and to doubt it is nothing but obstinacy. The Qur'an brings this truth here in order to show that Allah has given man the faculties of understanding and reflection.

Wa ja'ala .................... wal-af'idah (76:32): "And He made for you hearing, sight and hearts [i.e., faculties of thought]." And what has man done upon receiving these blessings of Allah: this hearing, this sight and this power of reason? Look at man's conduct!

Qalilan ma tashkurun (76:32): "Yet you give little thanks."

The faculty of hearing and the faculty of sight are two wondrous miracles within the human self. Man has come to know some aspects of them. And by "al-af'idah" (hearts) the Qur'an points to the faculty of thought. This is the most wondrous of wonders. Man has still not been able to acquire complete knowledge about the faculty of reason. Reason is a unique miracle of Allah within man.

Modern sciences have discovered some astonishing facts about the faculty of hearing, and it is appropriate to mention some of them here.

"Our sense of hearing begins its work from the outer ear, and none but Allah knows where its end lies. Scientists say that sound produces waves in the air, and these waves travel to the ear. The ear organizes them so that they fall upon the eardrum, and thus the sound reaches the depth on the other side of the eardrum. This depth is such that in it there are spring-like round canals, which are in the shape of semicircles. In the part of these round canals there are four thousand arches, which are attached to the hearing apparatus of the head."

"The question is: what is the length of each arch, what is its volume, and how were these arches made, whose number runs into thousands, and how are they placed in such a small space, while besides them there are other bones which move like waves? And all this equipment is in a small hollow space behind the eardrum! In the ear there are one hundred thousand (one lakh) auditory cells! And at the end of the auditory nerves there are the finest fibres, whose very fineness is astonishing, and the mere thought of it makes the head spin."
(Allah aur Jadid Uloom, Abd al-Razzaq Nofal, p. 75)

"Look at the human sense of sight: at its centre there are 031 million (31 lakh) cells that receive light. These receiving eyes are the ends of nerves, and the important parts of the eye are the cornea, the choroid (Plancenta) and the retina (Ratina). These important organs are apart from thousands of nerves and centres."
(Ibid., p. 85)

After this it is explained that Allah, in creating man, did not give him these characteristics in vain, nor did this happen by chance without any will or plan. Rather, they were given so that man may live his life on this earth, and then on the Day of Recompense he may be called to account for his life and be rewarded or punished.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verse 24:

﴿Say: It is He who created you and made you multiply upon the earth, and to Him you shall be gathered.﴾

The Arabic word al-dharʾ (ذرء) means that a thing increases, and the meaning includes spreading out along with increasing. Al-hashr (الحشر) means gathering, that is, gathering after dispersal. In terms of imagery, these two are opposing or different movements, and in meaning they stand in contrast to each other. One meaning carries the idea of increase and scattering and spreading across the earth, while the other presents the scene of gathering and raising up. In a single verse, Allah combines both scenes so that both come into human awareness. This is the Quranic conception. Human beings, who keep spreading and dispersing across the earth, should remember that there is also a day of their gathering, when you will be gathered and raised up together in one place. After this life and this death, that is a very great matter.

“Then it is said: 'Are you in doubt about this great matter, and do you raise questions?'

﴿And they say, 'When will this promise be fulfilled, if you are truthful?'﴾

This is a doubt-laden question, and within it there is also a scent of obstinacy and arrogance.

Our knowledge of this promise and of the time of the Resurrection is such that it cannot come earlier or later than its appointed time. Whether we know its time or not makes no difference. Yet the matter to understand is that it is the Day of Recompense. For us, what difference does it make whether it comes tomorrow or after many millions of years? Our life is a brief life. The real point is that it is coming, and preparation for it is necessary. You will certainly be raised in it, and there will be reward and punishment.

For this reason Allah has not informed anyone of its time, because what benefit is there in anyone knowing the time of the Resurrection? It has no connection with the practical life of a human being, nor with the commands that have been given to him. Rather, the wisdom lies in people in general not knowing the time of its occurrence; only Allah knows it.”

"Say: The knowledge of it is only with Allah; I am only a plain warner."

Here the distinction between Creator and creation is complete. The Being of Allah stands apart and distinguished: He has neither likeness nor partner. And exclusive knowledge becomes specific to Him alone, while all creation, the Messengers and the angels included, stands before Allah in reverence.

"Say: Its knowledge is only with Allah; I am only a plain warner." As in the Hadith of Jibril (ﷺ), where it is said: "The one questioned about it knows no more than the questioner" (al-mas'ul 'anha bi-a'lamu min al-sa'il). This knowledge belongs neither to the Messengers nor to the angels; the duty of the Messenger is only to warn.

These people used to ask about the Hour in a manner of doubt, and they were being answered by Allah in an absolutely definite manner. The Qur'an, in its particular style, gives the impression as though this Day has already arrived, that these people are on the field of gathering, and the Hour is upon them, and now this is what is taking place there.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 67, verse 27:

"When they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be darkened, and it will be said: 'This is what you used to call for.'" (67:27)

Note: the passage quoted here is from the commentary on verse 27 as presented in the Urdu text, which quotes 76:72 in its second citation.

[The Urdu text here begins with the verse "فلما راوہ" ("then when they see it"), and continues with the quotation "ھذا الذی کنتم بہ تدعون" ("This is that which you used to call for") (76:72).]

When they saw it, and it was before them, they had no expectation that it would stand before them. Now the shape of their faces is changing; clouds of grief are upon those faces. Now they are being rebuked in this manner.

"ھذا الذی کنتم بہ تدعون" (76:72): "This is that which you used to call for." Here it is, present and near. And your claim was: where is the Resurrection?

This manner, in which the Qur'an presents future events as though they have already occurred, is an excellent answer to their doubts and suspicions. They are given a conscious jolt: "Behold, the Resurrection is indeed established." The one who denied and doubted remains stunned before the Word of the Lord. He forgets that he is a denier; rather, he remains standing before the scene.

This depiction is effective because those scenes are, in God's knowledge, already present; in reality, those scenes are established, since God's knowledge is not confined within the bounds of time and place. Past, present and future belong only to humans. If God commands today, perhaps we too could see them in this way. Thus the deniers, the addressees, are suddenly transferred from the world to the Hereafter, and instead of doubt and suspicion they are made to confront it. They are brought before the reality which is established in God's knowledge; if He lifted the veil, we too would see it, but here God shows only its picture.

The polytheists of Makkah were so foolish, self-deluded and obstinate that they would wish for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the handful of believers to be destroyed, so that they would be relieved of concern about the believers. They would also counsel one another: "Brother, be patient; they are only a few, and they will perish, and then the discord which they have created within the ranks of Quraysh will end of its own accord." At times they were even caught up in the conceit that God would soon destroy Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, because they regarded them as sabians and misguided, since they were fabricating lies against God. Now, after this scene of gathering and resurrection, they are told: your wishes are well and good in their place, but if Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions were destroyed, how would you escape the painful punishment? Consider your conduct, your beliefs and your deeds. If this Prophet and his handful of companions were destroyed, what benefit would it bring you?

"Say: Have you considered: if Allah destroys me and those with me, or has mercy upon us, who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?" (Qur'an 67:28)

This is a question that invites serious reflection, and it is an invitation to consider your own affairs carefully, for your own good. Even if the Prophet and his small band of companions were to perish, what benefit would you gain? Allah remains. The Prophet and his companions are within the sphere of Allah's mercy. But you must go before Him. He created you, and to Him you will return. What is your preparation?

This is the context of the discourse. ﴿Who will protect the disbelievers...﴾ is said. It is not said "you are disbelievers," but rather "who will protect those who disbelieve?" The implication is that the punishment is for the disbelievers.

﴿Then who will protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?﴾ (76:82) This is the wise method of da'wah (the call to Islam). On one hand they are warned; on the other, a hint is given that they should turn back, lest they adopt the path of foolishness and be led to direct confrontation, which would leave them entangled in obstinacy.

Sometimes an allusive manner has more effect than an explicit one. ﴿We did not think that you had come from anywhere...﴾ Such a style is very effective.

Now, after this hint, the two positions are not equal. The believers have trust in their Lord. Having risen up relying upon Allah, they are content with their faith; they are certain that they are upon the path of guidance, and indeed it is their opposing party that is afflicted with manifest error.

This is why the attribute of al-Rahman is used in place of Allah here: Allah does not destroy the Prophet and his small band of companions, but is Merciful and Generous towards them, just as you would wish.

The Prophet ﷺ and his companions are instructed to strengthen their present bond with Allah, and to make the declaration:

"We have believed in Him" (76:92): "We believe in Him," solely in Allah. The manner of this speech shows that Allah is very close to the Muslims, and that there is a bond of trust between them.

"And upon Him we have relied" (76:92): "and upon Him is our reliance," solely upon Him. Allah commands the Prophet to announce this grace and generosity. It is as though he is being told not to fear the wishes and words of these disbelievers. "I am with you and with your companions." Therefore, let him make this announcement. This is Allah's declaration of friendship with the Prophet and the friends of the Prophet, in which there is honour for them.

Indirectly, the opposing party is also threatened:

"Soon you will know" (76:92): "Soon you will come to know who is in clear error."

This too is a manner that breaks through the fortresses of obstinacy and insistence, and compels the addressee to reflect upon his own position, lest he himself be astray, and lest he himself be deserving of punishment.

"Who will protect the disbelievers from the painful punishment?" (76:92): But throughout this discourse, Allah does not call them disbelievers, so that they do not become stubborn. This is the style of da'wah (invitation), which is beneficial in most circumstances.

And now, the final, severe blow upon the strings of intellect and reason, from which a resonance arises. It is indicated: beware, this is the punishment of the Hereafter, but Allah also punishes the disobedient in this world. If Allah were to withhold water today, consider what your condition would become.

Qul ara'aytum... (Say: Have you considered...) ... Mu'in

The word "ma'un ghawran" (67:30; 76:03) means water that has sunk deep into the veins of the earth and for which there is no means of bringing it back.

"Ma'in" (76:03) is the spring that gushes forth from the earth bringing water. These scenes they used to see constantly, though on that day they would doubt them. Yet the dominion of the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and He may dry up these springs whenever He wills. If Allah were to extract this very means of their livelihood, what would the consequences be? After this they are invited: "It is possible that this could happen; consider it carefully."

Thus this Surah concludes. These are arguments, impressions, and a tour of the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth; every verse is thought-provoking in itself, a stirring of the heart, sight, thought and imagination.

This is a highly thought-provoking Surah. Though its size is small, its concepts and guidance spread across the horizons of the universe. These are allusive arrows that carry thought and imagination very far and take one on a tour of the cosmos.

This Surah lays the foundations of the Islamic concept of life. It establishes within the conscience that all decisions were made in eternity (azal). Allah has complete control over the whole universe; human beings were sent here for trial and test, the result of which will emerge on the Day of Resurrection and Gathering. Perfection and beauty in Allah's creation are at their peak. Allah's knowledge encompasses the outward and the inward; provision is in Allah's hand. Allah is the guardian of creation, He is with His creation. What is a Muslim's conception now, and what is the relationship of this universe with Allah? This is the body of concepts upon which the structure of the Islamic system of life is raised. The believer's relationship with his Lord, the believer's relationship with his own self, the believer's relationship with his brothers and with mankind, the believer's relationship with all living creatures, the believer's relationship with the things of the earth's surface. These concepts give those relationships their detailed character in the human conscience. From this, the values and standards of a Muslim's life become clear.
